subject.title: Expose plugin approval APIs needed by external HITL plugins

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the linked public external-verification approval contract as the supported plugin SDK and Gateway boundary, subject to its security and upgrade review?
rationale: This is not a repair of an established contract: it adds a new authorization-capable plugin API, persistent approval lifecycle behavior, and client presentation flow. Automation cannot choose the permanent public boundary or the required level of production proof.

options.title: Sponsor the narrowed host-owned contract
options.body: Review and land the focused implementation only if its ownership checks, compatibility surface, and proof requirements meet the accepted RFC direction.

options.title: Defer the core API
options.body: Keep ordinary approval APIs unchanged and require the external verifier use a future, separately specified core seam.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrowed host-owned contract
recommendation.body: Review and land the focused implementation only if its ownership checks, compatibility surface, and proof requirements meet the accepted RFC direction.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior merged revert and the supplied accepted-RFC context make them the strongest available routing candidate for the public approval-boundary decision.
